clue.text: Perhaps security detail drove veteran back inside

indicators.note: inside places the reversed veteran within the herd word

parts.note: a drove is a herd of animals, as is a pack

indicators.note: back tells us the word for veteran is read in reverse

parts.note: a veteran is old

explanation.surface: A security guard's job description: he drove an old soldier back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps security' is the definition by example; 'detail' and 'drove' look like a security squad's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A padlock is one example of a device that provides security, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Field doctor tears up

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor in the field weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field doctor' looks like an army medic; 'doctor' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasture is grassland for grazing, a field.

clue.text: First to do drug trials can't stand

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of do
E is ecstasy
trials are tests

explanation.surface: A patient who loathes being first in line for drug trials.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to loathe it, so to be unable to bear it.

clue.text: Work in parade essentially supporting opening of Olympic Games

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below the earlier pieces
opening of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of Olympic
PE, physical education, is school games

indicators.note: essentially means the essence, the middle letters of the word

parts.note: the two middle letters of parade

explanation.surface: The work at the heart of an Olympic opening ceremony parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Opus, Latin for work, gives opera, so an opera is a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music, so a work in the arts sense.

clue.text: Note bad luck to interrupt monarch with subordinate yielding to pressure

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into the monarch word

parts.note: a king is a monarch

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of luck are spoilt, so they are rearranged

parts.note: under means lower in rank, subordinate

explanation.surface: A king's bad luck is that a junior official gives in under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To knuckle under is an idiom for submitting or giving in, so knuckling under is yielding under pressure.

clue.text: Guilty can use the camp beds once stripped

indicators.note: once stripped tells us every word in the run loses its outer letters, leaving only the middle

parts.note: can stripped of its first and last letters
use stripped of its first and last letters
the stripped of its first and last letters
camp stripped of its first and last letters
beds stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone feels bad about borrowing camp beds once the bedding has been stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letter from each of can, use, the, camp and beds, and keep what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ashamed is feeling guilty about something you have done; the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Amazing ace, obvious spin with no fault seen

indicators.note: amazing suggests letters thrown into confusion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator praising an ace with obvious spin that was not called out.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis scene points to a fault call, but the definition is about blamelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone above suspicion is so trusted that nobody sees any fault or wrongdoing in them.

clue.text: Structures with many layers

parts.note: layers reads as strata or tiers, but means birds that lay eggs

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests multi-storey buildings; the layers are egg-laying hens.
explanation.definitionFit: Coops for laying chickens are structures holding many egg producers.

clue.text: Fury following low fee paid by bank?

indicators.note: following means the fury word comes after the low word

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
fury is rage

explanation.surface: Anger at a low fee charged by a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is a river bank, where a boat ties up, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the charge for mooring a boat, a fee paid for a berth alongside the bank.

clue.text: Least inspiring and stupidest students replacing doctor

indicators.note: replacing means the students take the place of the doctor in the word

parts.note: dumbest means stupidest
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
L is a learner, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: A ranking of the dullest, dimmest medical students.
explanation.definitionFit: The dullest thing is the most boring, the one that inspires least interest.

clue.text: Staff wearing station uniform get limited fare?

indicators.note: wearing puts the staff inside the word for station, as if clothed by it

parts.note: to station something is to set it in position
staff are the people employed, the men

explanation.surface: Railway staff in station uniform get only restricted fares on the trains.
explanation.walkthrough: U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet. 'Fare' means food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: A set menu offers a restricted choice of dishes at a fixed price, so the food on offer is limited.

clue.text: Member of parliament penning article on non-governmental organisation's blunder

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the owl word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a group of owls is called a parliament, so an owl is a member of one

indicators.note: on means the article is placed after the organisation's letters

parts.note: NGO is the usual abbreviation for a non-governmental organisation
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An MP writes an article attacking a charity's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' is not an MP: a parliament is the collective noun for owls.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal is a football goal scored against your own side, and figuratively any self-inflicted blunder.

clue.text: Incredible Hulk's ace new release

indicators.note: incredible suggests something wildly changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: A puff for the new release of an Incredible Hulk comic or film starring a crack hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incredible Hulk' is the comic character's full name, but 'Incredible' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unshackle someone is to free them from chains, so to release them.

clue.text: Harangue Oscar judge

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet
to rate something is to judge its worth

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner's speech berates the judging panel.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak pompously at length, much as a harangue is a long ranting address.

clue.text: Stand that supports hire cycles

indicators.note: cycles means the letters go round, the first moving to the end

parts.note: to lease something is to hire it

explanation.surface: A rack that holds rental bicycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hire cycles' reads as bikes for rent; 'cycles' is a verb telling you to move the first letter to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that props up a painting or blackboard, a stand that supports it.

clue.text: Something Hollywood might produce in Los Angeles, California filling principally religious channel

indicators.note: principally means the first letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of religious

indicators.note: filling means California goes inside the channel word

parts.note: a dyke is a ditch or drainage channel
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A Hollywood production set in LA with a religious TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollywood is not the film industry but Paul Hollywood, a judge on the TV show The Great British Bake Off. Lardy cake is a traditional English sweet bread made with lard.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker such as Paul Hollywood might bake this traditional sticky bread, so it is something he might produce.

clue.text: Adamant Berlin's is ten times smaller at both ends

indicators.note: the phrase is cut down at both its start and its end, leaving a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run straight through these words once the outer ones are trimmed

explanation.surface: Someone insists that Berlin is ten times smaller than claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim the first four letters and the last four from the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insistent refuses to back down, which is what being adamant means.

clue.text: See 5
Cryptically goes for Batman and Robin, say

parts.note: read cryptically, the answer is an instruction: alter the word egos and you get goes

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's aside on how to clue the caped crusaders.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay, and 'goes' is what it produces. Bruce Wayne's alter ego is Batman; Dick Grayson's is Robin.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman and Robin are the secret second identities of their wearers, which is what an alter ego is.

clue.text: Clean and jerk holding up when used with energy and power

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means the jerk word sits under the rest, supporting it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A weightlifter's clean and jerk, done with energy and power.
explanation.walkthrough: The clean and jerk is a weightlifting lift; 'jerk' is in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from germs, sterile, so clean in a medical sense.

clue.text: For example spaghetti junction's highest point over city motorway

parts.note: the top is the highest point
O is over in cricket scoring
NY is New York City

explanation.surface: Spaghetti Junction's highest point rises above the city motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti Junction is the nickname of a tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham, England. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A toponym is a place name, and Spaghetti Junction is the popular name of a place.

clue.text: Capital city, south of Iowa

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: A geography quiz asking for a capital south of Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Daft place to go climbing in skates for example

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the fish

parts.note: skates are flat fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: the place to go is a euphemism for the loo, the toilet

explanation.surface: A silly place to go rock climbing is on ice skates.
explanation.walkthrough: Skates are taken as ice skates, but they are fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish and daft are both informal words for silly.

clue.text: Assistance as airline served up coffee on the counter

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: on the counter suggests running counter, read the other way

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: An airline serves coffee from the counter as a help to passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Abettal is a rare noun for abetment, helping someone, so assistance.

clue.text: Vacuous politician going through the escort agency's terms

indicators.note: going through places the politician inside the run of end letters
terms are ends or limits, so take the last letter of each word

parts.note: the last letters of the and escort
an MP is a Member of Parliament
the last letter of agency, its term, with the 's read as belonging to it

explanation.surface: A shallow MP is reading the small print of an escort agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' looks like contract conditions but means the ends of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty here means lacking meaning or thought, which is what vacuous describes.

clue.text: Elon Musk's angry about sanctimonious left hiding where some plans go?

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the word for sanctimonious
angry suggests the letters are thrown about in a rage and rearranged
hiding means the letter for left is put out of sight

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Elon Musk is cross about a self-righteous left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Musk stands for 'is'. Musk's own plans, from rockets to cars, give the surface its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Failed schemes are said to go up in smoke, vanishing like burnt paper; the question mark marks the idiom.

clue.text: See 4
Drink beer occasionally — excellent

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: occasionally means take only some of the letters, every other one

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker's verdict on a sip of beer now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is a slightly dated informal word for wonderful or very good.

clue.text: Aquarium commercial including introduction from Rick Stein?

parts.note: an aquarium is a fish tank

indicators.note: including means the advert takes in the next letter

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, AD

indicators.note: introduction from means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of Rick

explanation.surface: An advert for a fish tank fronted by TV chef Rick Stein.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick Stein is a British TV cook famous for seafood; here 'Stein' alone is the definition, a German beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large beer mug, an example of a tankard, so the question mark is needed.

clue.text: This writer's books receiving hype with Independent publishing house

indicators.note: receiving tells us the books come after the hype and Independent pieces they take on

parts.note: this writer's means the setter is, I'M
PR is public relations, hype
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A writer boasts that his books get hype from an independent publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' stands for I'M, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a brand name under which a publisher issues books, often a house within a larger firm.

clue.text: MC Hammer ultimately going to back companion

indicators.note: the letter is shifted to the rear of the word

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, is a compere

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, the last letter of Hammer

explanation.surface: The rapper MC Hammer eventually supports a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MC Hammer' reads as the rapper, but MC is COMPERE and Hammer only supplies its last letter R, which 'going to back' moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is an equal or associate, a fellow or comrade of the same standing.

clue.text: Somehow warn Harry, one has a point

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Harry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Someone must find a way to tell Harry that someone has a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a point' sounds like conceding an argument; it means a creature with a spike.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale whose male bears a long spiral tusk, so it literally has a point.
